## 255. The slice-23 review's four cases (2026-10-09)

(The driver's dispositions of the Reviewer's S1 to S4 on `build/m4-s23`; D4 §§2.4, 4.3, 5.3, 6.1, 7.1, 7.4, 9.2; E110, E111, E121 CD2. Cases in M302, M304 and M305; `../COVERAGE.md`, "M4 slice 23: the review's four cases".)

**What this pass changes in earlier sections.** Section 245's references: only `deploy/<name>`; a backend reference is refused (S4). Section 247's target gains `resources` (S3), and an applying effect changes units only. Section 250's reads gain the environment read below (S1).

**The environment read** (S1; D4 §6.1, A.2, A.8). **`GET /v1/projects/:p/environments/:e`** (`:e` the name) → **200** `{"environment": {…}}`, a stored read (no adapter call, no write). Pinned of the object: `last_verified`, `attempted` and `observed` as the environment record holds them (section 250); **`supervision`**, the running service's (D4 §9.2, A.2 `Supervision`): `attached` when its launch was granted by the running incarnation, **`unknown`** when it was granted by an earlier one (a service that survived an engine restart, E110), `null` when the environment has no service of its current generation recorded; and **`conditions`**, an array of D4 A.2's `EnvironmentReadCondition`, holding **`supervision_unknown`** exactly when `supervision` is `unknown`. While supervision is `unknown`, `observed.condition` is never `healthy` (E121 CD2); the `degraded` it reads under CD2 is written by the observation job (slice 27, M329 (e)), which slice 23 does not have. Not pinned: the read's other members.

**Supervision and verification** (S1; D4 §§4.3, 5.3). A round of a generation whose service's supervision is `unknown` is decided `unknown`, `missing` holding an entry of kind **`supervision`** (A.2 `VerificationMissing`), whatever its reads and checks; the environment record's `attempted.outcome` is `verification_unknown` and `last_verified` is not written; `alpha_complete` is not satisfied.

**A granted launch** (S2; D4 §2.4). "A launch for g granted" is the attempt's recorded grant (its `init_instance` recorded), which closing the launch at a restart does not undo: with g's unit gone the read is `partial` (`reconciled_partial`), and no further attempt starts without the human's `rollout_partial` answer. The decision's form is not pinned here.

**The mapping beyond units** (S3; D4 §2.4, D4-A03). Section 247's `resources` are in the inventory reconcile reads, and the engine maps them: a populated domain cgroup, a socket or a directory left after a teardown is `partial`, never `applied`; a resource whose state is `unread` is `unknown`; a prefixed unit no intent names, in any state (`failed` included), is `conflicting` in a teardown as in a deploy; a deploy's g with no unit but a populated domain cgroup is not `absent`; a `prior` unit whose `invocation_id` or `instance` is not the one frozen in the attempt's capability is not "prior exactly as frozen", so not `absent`. Where D4 leaves `partial` against `conflicting` or `unknown` to the mapping, the cases assert only "neither `absent` nor `applied`".

| What | Fixed as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `resources` on the scripted target † | section 247's Resource | D4 §2.4 names cgroups, sockets and directories in the inventory; the scripted target held units only |
| An applying effect and `resources` † | units only | So a test can make a resource survive an effect |
| `supervision`, `conditions` on the environment read | as above | D4 §6.1 and A.2's names |
| The verification's missing kind | `supervision` | D4 A.2 `VerificationMissing` |
| References | `deploy/<name>` only | D4 §§7.1, 7.4; the driver's ruling on S4 |

## 256. What the slice-24 tests assume throughout

(M4 plan §3.2, §2; BS4 §§4.1, 8, 9; E121, E122; written 2026-10-09 on `verify/m4-s24` from `main` at `7af0e5a`. Rows M307 to M313. Helpers: `deploy/host.mjs` (the sandbox lane and the operator's guard), `deploy/fixture-service.cjs` (the service), `deploy/target-check.mjs` (the post-deploy check program), `deploy/kernel.mjs` (slice 23's, whose `deployable` gains `entries` and `governed`).)

- **Files and lanes.** Kernel lane, on section 247's scripted adapter: `M308-the-projection-and-its-mappings`, `M309-sealing-modes-and-bounded-preparation`, `M312-unsupported-configurations-refused`. Sandbox lane, on the real `local_service` adapter: `M307-the-deployment-journey-on-a-real-unit`, `M308-the-projection-on-the-target`, `M309-modes-through-the-target-read`, `M310-the-service-profile`, `M311-identity-from-the-target`, `M311-the-identity-reads-duration`, `M312-unsupported-configurations-on-the-host`, `M313-nothing-of-the-operators`. The manifest lists the kernel files first and the files whose instruments act (M310, M311) last (BS4 §4.1 rule 9).
- **A sandbox-lane engine** is section 122's (`sandboxEngine`, the host checks run, the user manager reached through `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`) started with **`--harness-deploy-adapter real`** (section 247) on every start, the first included. The engine does not refuse to start without the switch (`scripted` is the harness default, so M1 to M3 engines start unchanged): the harness adds the switch to every start and reads back from the started engine that it selected `real` (section 264). The adapter is qualified by section 248's fixture (the stand-in of BS4 §8; M307 (f) without it is slice 29's). The check runner is qualified by section 181's fixture, so the project's checks run in real `check` domains (section 182).
- **The deployable project on the host** (`hostDeployable`): T1; its governed file names two check programs, `probe` (section 182's) and `target` (section 258's), both under the test's own directory and in `runner_config.direct.read_paths`; checks `acc` (acceptance, R1.1) and `smoke`, both `probe exit 0`, and `behaves`, the required `post_deploy_behavior` check of the `alpha_complete` scope (`requires` `["environment", "artifact_digest"]`), `target --hold go --release-dir <dir>`; the revision's `server.js` is the fixture service; one stage, built by a scripted Builder that asks for the nomination; the workspace checks recorded by the engine. Each environment is configured by section 245's route with `configContent` and a port free on the host, `env` `{"SURETY_TEST_HOST_NS", "MARK"}` (section 258).
- **The candidate stays `developing`** wherever a file deploys it more than once (M310, M311, M313, M311 (h)): their rounds' checks exit 1 unless the case needs a `verified` row. Whether a candidate already `alpha_deployed` may be deployed again, to the same or another environment, is not pinned (D4 does not say; a question for Sean, section 263).
- **Order of setup** (BS4 §4.1): the operator's guard (section 257) is taken first; then the engine; nothing the test itself creates on the host (M313's decoys) exists before the file's engine has deployed a real unit.
- **No result from a fixture.** Every check result names an execution the engine registered; in the sandbox lane every one is the engine's own observation of a real check domain.

## 257. Unit names, host reads, the test's own acts, and the operator's guard (M313)

(BS4 §4.1 rules 1, 2, 4, 7, 8; D4 §§9.3, 9.5; E64; section 141.)

- **Names.** As section 250: `surety-<h>-<env>-g<n>.service`, `<h>` the first 12 hex digits of SHA-256 of `$SURETY_HOME` as the engine is given it, `<env>` the environment's id (`env_<ULID>`). A test's own unit matches `^surety-<h>-env_<ULID>-g[1-9][0-9]*\.service$` with its own `<h>` (`ownUnitPattern`).
- **Host reads** (read only): `systemctl --user show -p <props> -- <exact name>`; `systemctl --user list-units --all --no-legend --plain --full` with no pattern, filtered by the test in JavaScript (a listing grants nothing); `systemctl --user is-system-running`; the unit's cgroup files under `/sys/fs/cgroup` + its `ControlGroup`; `/proc/<pid>/{stat,status,exe,cmdline,environ,mountinfo,cgroup,fd,net/dev,net/unix,ns}`; the walk of `/proc/<pid>/root/surety/app`; `journalctl --user -u <exact name> -o cat`.
- **The test's own acts on a unit**, each by its exact name only, and only for a name of the test's own prefix that an attempt intent of the test's own store names (`create_units`): `systemctl --user stop`, `restart` and `reset-failed`. A restart (M311 (c), (d)) is made only after `assertServiceContained`: the unit is loaded, its `ControlGroup` is its own, the recorded application pid is the same process (its start time) in that cgroup's tree and in its `cgroup.procs`, and in none of the host's pid, network and mount namespaces. A stop is made where the engine cannot tear the unit down (an ambiguous attempt holds the lease, M311 (a)). Nothing stops, restarts, reloads, re-executes or daemon-reloads the user manager; nothing touches Docker or the system manager.
- **Decoys** (M313 (a)): `sdlcx-decoy-<12 hex>.service`, outside every Surety prefix, and `surety-<h2>-<env>-g1.service`, `<h2>` derived from a second disposable directory the test makes and `<env>` one of the file's own environment ids. Each is created by `systemd-run --user --unit=<exact name> --collect` running `/usr/bin/sleep 3600` with `MemoryMax=16M`, `TasksMax=2`, after reading its `LoadState` `not-found` (a name in use is refused), and stopped (and reset if failed) by its exact name.
- **The operator's guard** (`operatorGuard`; row M313's before-and-after check, at the end of **every** slice-24 file, kernel files included). Before: `is-system-running` prints `running` (else the file fails before anything), the loaded units, `/tmp/surety-*` and `/dev/shm/surety*`. After, each finding reported by exact name and failing the file: the manager not `running`; a unit of a tracked home's prefix still loaded (it is then stopped by its exact name if the store's intents name it); a cgroup directory of that prefix under `user@<uid>.service`; a file under `$SURETY_HOME/run/` whose name carries one of the home's environment ids or its prefix; a decoy still loaded (then removed by its exact name); a `.service` unit that was `active` before, other than a Surety home's or a decoy, no longer `active` †; a new `/tmp/surety-*` or `/dev/shm/surety*` that is not one of the file's own directories. It never cleans by pattern.

- **An idle socket-activated service** (2026-10-10; the coordinator's ruling after slice 26's runs on the Builder's build, where `snapd.session-agent.service` exited idle during M324's sandbox file). The guard's "a unit outside the prefix changed state" finding is waived for a `.service` only when every one of these holds: (1) read after the file with `systemctl --user show` of its exact name, it is `loaded` and `inactive` `dead`, never `failed`; (2) its `TriggeredBy` names one or more units, each a `.socket`; (3) each of those sockets is `active` in the guard's before listing, the before snapshot taken at the file's start, and `active` in its after listing. Anything else keeps the finding: `failed`, not loaded, no `TriggeredBy`, a trigger that is no socket, a socket that changed state or cannot be read, or a read that fails. A waived change is still reported, as a `# note:` line naming the unit and its sockets, never in silence.
## 258. The fixture service and the post-deploy check program

- **The fixture service** (`deploy/fixture-service.cjs`, committed as `server.js`; CommonJS, Node's own modules). It listens on `127.0.0.1:$PORT`. Routes: `GET /hello` → 200 `{"ok", "mark", "pid", "argv", "cwd", "port"}`; `GET /version` → 200 a made-up revision; `GET /probe` → 200 its start-up probes; `GET /act/<mode>` → a guarded act, 403 `{"refused": [reasons]}` when its guard refuses. At start, and only when its guard passes, it tries to write `/surety/app/.probe-write` and `/surety/.probe-write` and to rename `/surety/app` (each must fail), writes `/surety/home/fixture-marker` and `/surety/state/fixture-marker`, and writes `/tmp/fixture-marker` only if absent, with a value of its own start; it prints `APP-OUTPUT-<MARK>-stdout` and `…-stderr` once listening. Acts: `exit`, `detach` (a child of its own, detached, every stream closed, listening on the same port for at most 120 s, then the application exits), `exec-program` (`execve /usr/bin/sleep 120`), `exec-args` (the runtime, other arguments), `reexec-same` (the runtime, the identical argument vector), `title` (`process.title`), `fill-tmp` (64 KiB blocks into `/tmp/fill` until refused or 8 MiB), `fill-inodes` (empty files under `/tmp/inodes` until refused or 4,096), `print-marker`. **Its guard** (E64's instrument half, section 141's form): `SURETY_TEST_HOST_NS` (`pid:[n],net:[n],mnt:[n]`, the test's own namespaces) differs from its own in all three, `/proc/1/comm` is no system init, at most 16 processes visible; any failed read refuses. No act signals anything.
- **The post-deploy check program** (`deploy/target-check.mjs`, installed with a shebang naming the test's `node`). With `--hold <name> --release-dir <dir>` it waits (at most 280 s) for `<dir>/<name>`, whose JSON content is its plan `{"get": [<path>…], "exit": <n>}`; it asks `SURETY_TARGET_APP` for each path (one GET, 15 s), writes `SURETY-TARGET-REPORT {"target", "results": [{"path", "status", "body", "error"}], "plan"}` and exits with the plan's `exit`. It signals nothing, starts nothing and connects only to the address its environment names.
- **The release** (the test's half): the test writes the plan only after reading the service's containment (`assertServiceContained`, section 257) whenever the plan names an act; it removes the file once the round's verification row exists, so the next round holds again.
- **A second hold** (objections 036 and 037, 2026-10-10): a plan may carry `"then": "again"`; after asking for its paths the program waits (at most 280 s) for `<dir>/again`, a second plan `{"get", "exit"}` naming no act, asks for its paths and exits with its `exit`; the report then carries `plan2`. The test writes it only after the fact the case waits for is read from the host (`hostUntil`, no engine tick): for M311 (b), a `--detached-child` process in the unit's cgroup holding a listening socket on `127.0.0.1:<port>` (`listenerOf`: `/proc/<pid>/net/tcp` and `/proc/<pid>/fd`) while the application runs, then the application gone; for M311 (f), the application (same pid and start time) listening again on a new socket. Both files are removed with the verification row. **`detach`** exits 1 s after its child answers on the port (at most 10 s after starting it). **`reexec-same`** re-executes with the vector of `/proc/self/cmdline` (Node makes `process.argv[1]` absolute, so `process.argv` is not the start command).

## 259. The service domain, the launch and the identity read, as the tests read them

(D4 §§3.4, 5.2, 9.2, A.3; J2; E110; E121 item 4.)

- **What runs.** The service's working directory is `/surety/app`; `start[1..]` are paths relative to it †; its environment holds `PORT` (the configured port) † and the configuration's `env` variables. `local_service` takes the one target `app`; an environment-bound check's environment holds **`SURETY_TARGET_APP`** `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, a port in the check's own network namespace (D4 §5.2).
- **The attempt, in host terms** †: `init_instance` `{pid, start_time}` and `app_instance` `{pid, start_time, exe, exe_sha256, argv}`, `pid` the **host** pid, `start_time` field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat` as an integer, `exe` the configured runtime's path, `exe_sha256` the SHA-256 of `/proc/<pid>/exe`'s bytes, `argv` `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (the start command). Written once (`app_instance` at the init's `started`), never rebound. The init is the launcher's (`MainPID`'s) child with innermost `NSpid` 1; the application is the init's child.
- **`deploy.launch_authorized`**, once per granted launch †: `subject` `{attempt, environment, operation, domain}`; `payload` `{"init": {pid, start_time}, "limits": {"memory_max", "memory_swap_max", "pids_max"}}`, the limits read back from the unit's cgroup files before the grant, in bytes and tasks.
- **The service domain** (`execution_domains`, D4 A.3): `attempt` set (and `invocation`, `check_execution` null); `cgroup_path` `/sys/fs/cgroup` + the unit's `ControlGroup` (the domain cgroup is the unit's own, E121 item 4); `state` as A.4 (`terminated` once closure is observed); **`reservation`** `{"memory": service_memory_max, "check_capacity": <the memory a check domain is admitted at: the effective domain_memory_max>}` † as JSON.
- **The unit** (host-read): `Delegate=yes`, `Restart=no`, `MemoryMax` = `service_memory_max`, `MemorySwapMax=0`, `TasksMax` = `service_tasks_max`; `MainPID` the launcher; its journal carries none of the application's output.
- **Runtime files** †: every socket and directory the engine makes for a service domain or its link lies under `$SURETY_HOME/run/` and carries the environment's id (or its prefix) in its name, so the guard and M307 (e) can find any left.
- **Identity reads** (`deployment_verifications.identity_reads`, section 250) gain † **`duration_ms`**, the read's elapsed time as the engine measured it (M311 (h)), and **`detail`**, null on `match`, otherwise an object whose `field` names what did not hold; CD4's case pins `field` `argv` for arguments that differ (M311 (g)). `instance.pid` is the host pid.

## 260. The artifact: the canonical manifest, the bounds, and what is left on disk

(D4 §3.1, A.2, A.6, A.7; E117; BS4 §11.3 as approved; rows M308, M309; the slice-23 review's minor m5.)

- **The canonical manifest and digest** †: the manifest is the array of entries `[path, "file", mode, size, sha256]`, one per regular file of the projection, `path` relative with `/` separators, `mode` `"100755"` when the file is executable in the revision and `"100644"` otherwise, `size` in bytes, `sha256` 64 lower-case hex digits of the bytes; sorted by `path` in code-unit order (byte order for the ASCII paths the tests use). `artifact_digest` is `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the manifest's JSON text with no whitespace (`JSON.stringify` of the array). A test computes it from any walk of the tree (the sealed copy, or `/proc/<pid>/root/surety/app`) and compares. `artifacts.entries` is the manifest's length, `artifacts.bytes` the sum of its sizes.
- **Excludes**: an entry of `artifact.exclude` names a path; it excludes that file, or that directory and everything under it (with or without a final `/`). `.surety/` is always excluded.
- **Bounds**, each inclusive: a projection of exactly `artifact_max_entries` entries, or exactly `artifact_max_bytes` bytes, passes †. `artifacts_max_bytes` bounds the `bytes` of every `artifacts` row of the home plus the new one. **`--harness-artifact-free-bytes <n>`** (harness mode only; a usage error otherwise, as every harness flag) makes artifact admission take `<n>` as the free bytes of the engine home's filesystem; admission refuses when the new artifact would leave less than `host_reserve_disk` free †. `artifact_prepare_deadline` is measured on the engine's clock from the start of the request's preparation, and checked at least once after the barrier below.
- **A refusal at the request** †: **422 `artifact_refused`**, `subject.refusal` the A.2 `ArtifactRefusal` (`symlink`, `submodule`, `special_file`, `too_many`, `too_large`, `retention_full`, `disk_reserve`, `prepare_deadline`); one `artifact.failed` with `payload.refusal`; no authorization recorded, no work item. **A sealed copy that does not rehash** when a request would reuse it: **409 `artifact_corrupt`**, nothing authorized; at an effect's precondition, section 250's fact `artifact_integrity`. Either way the `artifacts` row becomes `failed`, one `artifact.failed` with `payload.reason` `artifact_corrupt` †, and one finding `category` `security`, `effective_severity` `high`, `scope` `project`, `status` `open`.
- **A special file** †: no git tree can hold one (git's modes are 100644, 100755, 120000, 160000 and 040000; any other is shown canonicalized), so M308 (b)'s special file is read as one placed in a sealed copy (a FIFO): the next request reusing the copy is refused `artifact_corrupt`, the FIFO never opened and never omitted.
- **A sealed copy deleted** † (M308 (c), D4-I01's "projecting again, after deletion"): the next request that seals the same projection makes it again, under the same digest, at the recorded artifact's path, with no second `artifacts` row. (The alternative, refusing it as corrupt, is Sean's to choose; section 263.)
- **What is left on disk** (m5 and D4-I08) †: after any request (issued, coalesced, refused at the gate, refused `config_secrets_changed`, `config_invalid` or `artifact_refused`), a cancellation, or a kill and a restart followed by one tick, every entry under `$SURETY_HOME/artifacts/` lies within the `path` of an `artifacts` row, and the rows' `bytes` stay within `artifacts_max_bytes`. A request seals an artifact only if it will use it, or records what it sealed. **A cancelled preparation** is read as the engine's orderly stop (SIGTERM) while it prepares †; a killed one as the barrier's `kill`.
- **Barrier `artifact.staging_written`**: after every projected file is written into the staging directory, before its write bits are removed and it is renamed (section 18's rules).

## 261. Unsupported configurations (M312)

(D4 §§3.2, 9.2, 10 X2, Appendix B; Q4; E120 item 2.)

- **At `PUT …/config`** (section 245): `persistent_state` (any value but absent or `false`), a non-empty `egress`, `targets` empty or of two, an `adapter` other than `local_service`, and a `build` step are each **422 `config_invalid`** with `subject.field` the key's name (`persistent_state`, `egress`, `targets`, `adapter`, `build`) †; no version and, for a new name, no environment written. Whether the engine knows `persistent_state` and `build` as keys refused in M4 or as unknown keys is its own.
- **At the request** †, before any authorization row and any intent: a `runtime.path` absent from the host (`subject.field` `runtime.path`); a runtime whose bytes' SHA-256 is not `runtime.sha256` (`runtime.sha256`); a start command whose entry point is not in the sealed artifact, or which names an absolute host path (the project's checkout, the operator's home) (`start.1`); one whose program is not `runtime.path` (`start.0`): each **422 `config_invalid`**. No authorization, no work item, no operation, no adapter call; with the real adapter no unit of the environment's prefix, and nothing of the checkout run or mounted by any process the test can read.

## 262. Barriers and faults of slice 24

Section 33's rules for barriers (arming while the engine runs, `pause` and `kill`, one firing per arming). Faults are harness-only, one-shot, of the real adapter, armed per environment.

| Name | Fires, or does |
|---|---|
| `artifact.staging_written` | section 260 |
| `adapter.before_host_call` | in an effect call (`deploy`, `teardown`), after `adapterCall`'s capability check has passed and before the adapter's first host call |
| `deploy.round_registered` | after the transaction that registers a round (its bindings frozen, dependent evaluations stale), before its first identity read |
| `identity.between_halves` | in every identity read of the real adapter, after the first half of the stable snapshot (the unit's `ControlGroup` and `InvocationID`, the init's and the application's pid and start time) and before the executable, arguments, mounts and tree are read |
| `POST /v1/harness/deploy/faults` `{"environment": "env_…", "fault": "init_report_altered"}` → **200** † | the environment's next init `started` report is altered at the engine's receiving end to name the init's own pid (1) in place of the application's |
| `… {"fault": "identity_start_time"}` † | the environment's next identity read takes the application's start time read from `/proc/<pid>/stat` as one more than it is: the recorded start time no longer matches the pid (M311 (c); a reused pid cannot be made on demand) |
| `… {"fault": "identity_proc_unreadable"}` † | in the environment's next identity read, every read of the application's `/proc/<pid>/…` fails as `EACCES` (M311 (e); the host uid can read any process of the user namespaces it owns) |

Another fault name, or an unknown environment, is **400** `invalid_value`. Harness-only (section 7; M336 (b)).

## 264. The slice-24 review's S1, and the sandbox lane's adapter read back (2026-10-10)

(The driver's dispositions of the slice-24 Reviewer's S1 and deviation 4 on `build/m4-s24` at `9b2a25d`; D4 §3.1, A.7; D4-I08; BS4 §§4.1, 8. `../COVERAGE.md`, "M4 slice 24: the review's S1 and deviation 4".)

**What this pass changes in earlier sections.** Section 256's "an engine without the switch refuses to start" is withdrawn (below). Section 260's "what is left on disk" is read by real path.

**A recorded artifact under either spelling of the home** (S1; M309 (d)). `SURETY_HOME` may name the home through a symbolic link, and an engine may be started under one spelling after another engine of the same home was started under the other. Whatever spelling an `artifacts` row's `path` carries, the directory it names is the row's: no start sweep, request or cancellation removes it, unseals it, or changes a byte or a mode of it. The start sweep removes only what section 260 lets it remove: a staging directory (`artifacts/.staging-<16 hex>`, or slice 23's under a project), a digest directory (`artifacts/<project>/<64 hex>`) whose real path is no row's real path, and a project directory left empty with no row. The test's reading of section 260 (`unrecordedUnderArtifacts`) compares real paths: an entry is recorded when its real path is, or lies under, the real path of a row's `path`. How the engine canonicalises is its own; the case pins what survives. Not pinned: a running service's `/surety/app` read across such a restart (the kernel lane has no unit; the sandbox lane's M309 file reads the running tree).

**The sandbox lane's adapter** (deviation 4). The engine accepts `--harness-deploy-adapter` and, without it, runs the scripted adapter (section 247): it does not refuse to start, since refusing would break every M1 to M3 harness engine. So that no sandbox-lane file of slice 24 or later can pass on the scripted adapter, the harness makes and checks the switch: **`realAdapterStarts(fx)`** (`deploy/host.mjs`) wraps the fixture's `start`, adding `--harness-deploy-adapter real` to a start that names none and failing a start that names another value or names it twice; after each start it reads the engine's own argument vector (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` of the engine child; the spawned vector when the start was `until: 'none'` or the engine has exited) and fails unless it selects `real` by section 247's rule (`deployAdapterOf`, `assertRealAdapter`). `hostDeployable` applies it before its first start, so every start of its engine, a later restart included, is covered; a sandbox-lane file that builds its engine otherwise applies `realAdapterStarts` before its first start. Kernel-lane files keep the default.

| What | Fixed as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A row's directory under another spelling of the home † | never removed or changed; compared by real path | S1; D4-I08 "no referenced artifact is ever removed", A.7 |
| What the start sweep may remove † | staging; a digest directory whose real path is no row's; an empty project directory with no row | section 260, unchanged but for the comparison |
| The adapter of a sandbox-lane engine | the harness adds and reads back `--harness-deploy-adapter real` | deviation 4: the engine cannot refuse without breaking M2 and M3 |

## 265. What the slice-25 tests assume throughout

(M4 plan §3.3, §2; BS4 §§4, 8, 9; D4 §§5.1 to 5.3, 5.5, 4.5, 4.7; J7, J8, J9; E114, E115, E121 CD1; E126; written 2026-10-10 on `verify/m4-s25` from `main` at `8624e16`. Rows M314 to M319, and M305 (d) deferred here by slice 23. The slice-25 Builder's approved design, relayed by the driver 2026-10-10, is pinned in these sections; where this seam pins something else, the seam wins.)

- **Lanes and files.** Kernel lane, on §247's scripted adapter: `M305-a-result-invalidated-after-the-row`, `M315-bound-to-the-attempt-and-the-round`, `M316-bracketing-on-the-scripted-target`, `M317-verification-outcomes`, `M318-the-generation-guard`, `M319-capacity-reserved-at-admission`. Sandbox lane, on the real adapter (§§256, 264): `M319-the-reserved-check-capacity`, `M314-the-service-link`, `M316-bracketing-on-a-real-unit`. The manifest lists the kernel files first and the sandbox files last, the instrument files (`M314`, `M316-bracketing-on-a-real-unit`) last of all (BS4 §4.1 rule 9). Helpers: `deploy/rounds.mjs` (kernel and sandbox), `deploy/host.mjs` (sandbox, extended), `deploy/link-check.mjs` (the link-probing check program).
- **A round is the unit of verification** (D4 §5.3). Its `verification_rounds` row and its one `deployment_verifications` row are read as §250 gives them, through `roundsOf`, `roundRow`, `rowOf` and `verificationsOf`. A kernel-lane round's post-deploy executions are moved through the scripted check boundary (§190); a sandbox-lane round's are the engine's own observations of a real `check` domain.
- **The deploy-bound check tree** holds the protected inputs only, with an empty source projection (no candidate source): a `post_deploy_behavior` or `post_deploy_identity` check never sees `server.js` or `lib/greeting.js` (M314 (a); the Builder's design).
- **The clock and barriers.** The orchestration deadline and a round's own deadline are on the engine's clock, moved by §18's controlled clock (`advanceClock`). Barriers are armed as §33 and §251.

## 266. The re-verification route (`POST …/operations/:o/verify`)

(D4 §5.3 item 1, A.8; E114; the Builder's design.) **`POST /v1/projects/:p/operations/:o/verify`** with an empty body registers round k+1 of the operation's **latest attempt**: it freezes the round's bindings, marks the dependent `alpha_complete` evaluations stale, and puts the operation's orchestration stage back to `verification`, all in the request's transaction, before any identity read. It applies only to a **finalized deploy whose latest attempt succeeded**.

| Outcome | Answer |
|---|---|
| registered | **202** `{"round": {"id": "vr_…", "round": <k+1>, "operation", "attempt"}}` |
| not the project's, or no such operation | **404** `not_found` |
| not a verifiable operation (not a deploy, not finalized, the latest attempt not `succeeded`, or a teardown) | **409** `operation_not_verifiable`, a refusal body (§75: `code`, `reason`, `what_to_do`, `subject`); no round |

`verifyAgain` (rounds.mjs) is the 202 helper; `requestVerify` is the raw call. A round from this route has `origin` `operator` (§267).

## 267. Superseding rounds, and what a round freezes

(D4 §5.3 items 1, 7; E114; the Builder's design.) **`verification_rounds` gains** † `origin` (`finalizer` for the finalizer's first round, `operator` for a `POST …/verify` round, `supersession` for the round a change opens) and `lease` (the environment lease generation the round holds while it runs, §269). A round freezes, at registration (the `deploy.round_registered` barrier fires after it, before the first read): the candidate, mapping, operation, attempt, `deployment_generation`, `config_identity`, `protected_version`, the required check set (`required_checks`) and the `adapter_qualification` current at its start.

**Supersession.** A change to the round's effective `protected_version` or its required check set supersedes the open round: its `verification_rounds.status` becomes `superseded` with † **`superseded_reason`** `protected_change` (the version changed, the required set the same) or `required_set_changed` (the required set changed), and **`deploy.round_superseded`** names it (`subject.round`). **In the same transaction** a fresh round is registered, `origin` `supersession`, inheriting the superseded round's deadline, with its own fresh bracketing reads and registrations; no read or result of the superseded round is relabelled into it (the executions keep their own round in their trigger). The newest registered round decides; an earlier round's row, if any, is kept as history and never satisfies completion.

**Row invalidation** (§250; D4 §4.5). A `deployment_verifications` row that is not of the deciding round is recorded `round_superseded`; one whose `deployment_generation` is not the environment's current is recorded `generation_superseded`; a later attempt's invalidation stays `later_attempt`. The value is durable and written once (the `0017` triggers).

## 268. The service link and its log (row M314)

(D4 §5.1, §5.2; J8; the Builder's design.) An environment-bound check reaches the service only through the engine-brokered link: its environment holds `SURETY_TARGET_<NAME>` (for `local_service`, `SURETY_TARGET_APP`), and the engine relays each connection to the socket of the generation frozen on the execution. A connection to any other port or host has no route inside the check's namespace, so it never reaches the engine and is **not** in the link log; it is shown by the check's own report and a host read (the Builder's design).

- **`deploy/link-check.mjs`** is the test-owned link-probing check program (installed by `installLinkCheck` as the `check_command` **`link`**; `hostDeployable(..., {behaves: 'link'})` makes `behaves` run it with `--host-ns`). It fails closed (E64's instrument half): every step but `tree`, `get`, `hold` and `sleep` runs only when it reads its own containment from inside; the test writes its plan only after `assertCheckContained` has read the check's containment from the host (`releaseLink`). Its plan is `{"steps": [Step], "exit": <n>}`; it writes one line `SURETY-LINK-REPORT <json>` (`linkReport`) and exits with `exit`. Steps: `tree`, `get`, `reach` (a TCP attempt to a host:port), `unix`, `listen`, `open`/`wait_closed`, `unread`, `many`, `hold`, `sleep` (link-check.mjs documents each).
- **`service_link_log`** † is a `records` kind (added to `0017`'s RecordKind; the Builder adds it): one record **per execution**, its bytes JSON lines, one per connection the link relays, bounded by `egress_log_max_bytes` and linked from the result as `egress_log` is (`serviceLinkLogs` reads them). Each entry carries at least `execution`, `round`, `operation`, `attempt`, `generation`, `instance` (`{pid, start_time}`, the application instance), `decision` (`accepted` | `refused`), and, when a limit ended or refused it, `limit` `{key, value}` naming the `service_link_*` key. Values pass through the redactor.
- **The limits** (`service_link_connect_timeout`, `service_link_tunnel_max_seconds`, `service_link_tunnels_max`, `service_link_buffer_max_bytes`), lowered through the engine configuration: a tunnel past its max is closed, a connection past `service_link_tunnels_max` refused, each logged with its `limit`. The relay carries application data only: a reply grants no reverse connection, and a service reaches neither the engine nor the check.
- **`environment_unbound`** (D3 §5 X3, unchanged): a deploy-bound check from any non-deployment trigger records `environment_unbound`, with no environment, artifact or secret bound (M222 (c) pins it for a check the nomination, the operator route and a protected application register). A check of gate kind `alpha_complete` only is in no stage or `alpha_authorize` scope, so the operator route may instead refuse it (400 `invalid_value`, "not a required check of the candidate", as built in M3, section 180) †; M314 (g) accepts either, and in neither does it reach the link. M215's egress restrictions on D2's proxy are unchanged.

## 269. The generation guard under CD1 (row M318)

(D4 §4.5, §5.5; J9; E121 CD1; the Builder's design.) Every write that speaks for the environment checks its current generation, and for verification the deciding round, in its own transaction. CD1's re-verification round takes the **environment lease** again (its `lease` generation, §267): while a later deploy of the same environment holds the lease and has taken the next generation, an older operation's operator round waits (`environment_busy`) and registers no execution until the lease is free. When it then runs under a generation no longer current, its row is recorded with its computed outcome and `invalidated_reason` `generation_superseded` (`invalidated_at` set), writes neither `last_verified` nor `attempted`, and never satisfies `alpha_complete`; a late completion evaluation of that operation is refused `DEPLOY_GENERATION_SUPERSEDED`. The preempting-teardown form of M318 (a) is slice 27's (M327; COVERAGE.md).

## 270. Completion is evaluated after the row; the barrier before it (M305 (d), M315)

(D4 §4.3, §5.5; E114 item 3; the Builder's design.) The engine evaluates `alpha_complete` at the tick **after** the verification row is recorded (D1 §8.1 step 7), not in the row's transaction. **Barrier `deploy.before_completion`** † fires in that later tick, before the completion evaluation's transaction, so a case can act (or kill the engine) between a durable verified row and the advance. Completion does not trust a stored `verified` label (D4 §5.5): it re-reads the deciding results the row rests on. A deciding result invalidated (`check_results.invalidated_at`, correction 17) between the row and the evaluation refuses completion, not satisfied, with a reason naming the result or the row (`EVIDENCE_MISSING`, §249, or `DEPLOY_VERIFICATION_MISSING`); the candidate stays `developing`, and no automatic new round is registered. Every way the engine itself invalidates a deciding result needs ticks of the same project, which a barrier paused in that tick would hold, so M305 (d) drives the invalidation as a store write between incarnations (a kill at `deploy.before_completion`, the invalidation in the stopped store, a restart).

## 271. Verification capacity reserved at admission (row M319)

(D4 §4.7; E115 item 3; E126; the Builder's design.) A service domain takes no `max_concurrent_domains` slot; it holds its `service_memory_max` and `service_writable_bytes` from admission until its closure is observed, and while any service runs one check domain's capacity (`domain_memory_max`, `domain_writable_bytes`, one slot) is kept free and shared by post-deploy checks, which run serially. `execution_domains.reservation` is `{memory, check_capacity}` (§259). Only deployment-bound executions use the reserved capacity, and they are admitted first; other work is admitted beside them. A deploy whose service plus its reserved check does not fit waits for admission within the orchestration deadline, shown on the **deploy work item** as `dispatch_hold` `{"code": "resource_envelope", "subject": {"limit": …}}` (§168's work-read form, D4 A.2's WorkItem hold); reaching the deadline refuses it before the effect, naming `orchestration_deadline` (§250), the prior service untouched. Recovery restores a surviving service's reservation before any dispatch; its own supervision stays `unknown` (E110).

## 272. The slice-25 review's S1: the listing for another generation (2026-10-10)

(The driver's ruling on the slice-25 Reviewer's S1, on `build/m4-s25` at `81df5b9`; D4 §3.4 ("another generation `differs`"), §5.3 item 6; §262's faults. `../COVERAGE.md`, "M4 slice 25: the review's S1".)

**The rule.** The real adapter's identity read also lists the environment's prefix (read-only; §257's listing) to find whether another generation's unit is active, which makes the read `differs` naming `generation` (the slice-25 design). A listing that cannot be made (the call fails, passes its deadline or its output bound, or exits non-zero) leaves that fact unread, and the read is **`unread`**: `match` `unread`, `generation` `unread`, `detail` `{"field": "generation", "why": <naming the listing>}`. It is never left as it was: a `match` read with the listing failed is not a `match`. The round's row is then `unknown` (`missing` naming the `identity_read`), never `verified` (D4 §5.3 item 6: absent evidence is never read as success).

**The fault** †: **`POST /v1/harness/deploy/faults` `{"environment": "env_…", "fault": "identity_listing_failed"}` → 200**: in the environment's next identity read, the listing of the environment's prefix fails as a non-zero exit, without being made. One-shot, harness-only, as §262's other faults. M316 (d) on a real unit (`M316-bracketing-on-a-real-unit`) arms it while the round's check is held between the reads, so it falls on the second read.

## 273. What the slice-26 tests assume throughout

(M4 plan §3.4, §2; BS4 §§4.1, 8, 9; D4 §§2.4, 4.3 to 4.7, 9.2; E110 to E112, E115, E121 CD1 and CD3, E126, E127; written 2026-10-10 on `verify/m4-s26` from `main` at `5b680a9`. Rows M320 to M325; M306's unit of unknown ownership (deferred by slice 23) and M319 (c)'s dispatch-blocking form (deferred by slice 25). Helpers: `deploy/recover.mjs` (new: kills, barriers, reconcile reads, decisions on operations, invariants, the restored store), with `deploy/kernel.mjs`, `deploy/rounds.mjs` and `deploy/host.mjs` unchanged.)

- **Files and lanes.** Kernel lane, on §247's scripted adapter: `M320-reconcile-outcomes-on-the-scripted-target`, `M321-the-crash-matrix-on-the-scripted-target`, `M323-retry-after-reconcile`, `M324-a-restored-store-on-the-scripted-target`, `M325-the-lease-and-the-orchestration-deadline`, and one case added to slice 23's `M306-preconditions-before-the-effect`. Sandbox lane, on the real adapter (§§256, 264): `M320-reconcile-on-a-real-unit`, `M325-the-lease-held-until-the-links-close`, `M323-the-partial-retry-on-a-real-unit`, `M324-after-an-engine-restart-on-a-real-unit`, `M321-kills-with-a-real-service`, `M322-a-late-launcher-and-the-services-life`. The manifest lists the kernel files first, then the sandbox files whose only act is the engine's own, then those that kill the engine (M324, M321), and last M322, whose fixture acts and test restart act on a unit (BS4 §4.1 rule 9).
- **The scripted adapter, extended** (§247): an applying `deploy` also removes each unit its capability's `cleanup` names, as it removes each `prior` unit. Nothing else of §247 changes; its admission answer and its state survive a restart.
- **A sandbox file's policy.** Each sandbox file sets `deploy_auto_retries_max` 0 (so no automatic retry makes a second unit) and `service_memory_max` 64 MiB through the project's policy (§252), and keeps its candidate `developing` by ending its rounds' checks with exit 1, except where a case needs another outcome (§256).
- **No result from a fixture**, as §256. A kernel round's executions are moved through §190; a sandbox round's are the engine's own observations.

## 274. Kill points, barriers, the clock across a restart

(D4 §4.3; BS4 §4.1 rule 8; E64; sections 18, 33, 125, 251, 262.)

- **How a test kills its engine.** Two ways, and no other: (1) a barrier armed with `kill`, at which the engine sends SIGKILL to itself (§18); `killAt` (recover.mjs) asks for ticks until the engine has exited; (2) `killOwnEngine`, which sends SIGKILL through the `ChildProcess` handle the harness spawned (`fx.engine.kill()`, harness/engine.mjs), after reading `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (it names `serve`) and `/proc/<pid>/environ` (it holds `SURETY_HOME=<this test's home>`), and refuses if either read fails or disagrees. No test signals any other pid, a process group or `-1`. A restart is `fx.start()` on the same home; in the sandbox lane it carries the real-adapter switch (§264), and is followed by §181's and §248's qualification fixtures again (`startAgain`; objection 045): each start records a new host qualification (M110), so an adapter qualification recorded before it is no longer current (D4 §2.6) and a deployment after the restart would otherwise be refused `ADAPTER_UNQUALIFIED` for that alone (found showing slice 26's failures on `main` at `52f128c`).
- **Barriers added** (§18's rules; each fires once per arming; `pause` and `kill`):

| Name | Fires |
|---|---|
| `adapter.after_host_call` | in an effect call (`deploy`, `teardown`), after the adapter's host call returned (whatever it did), before the transition that records its receipt. In the kernel lane, after the scripted call made (or did not make) its change |
| `deploy.launch_granted` | after the transaction that grants a service launch (the attempt's `launch_state` `authorized`, `init_instance` recorded, `deploy.launch_authorized`), before the reply carrying the grant (and any secret) is written to the launcher. In the kernel lane, after the launch stand-in's grant (§247) |
| `init.app_started` † | when the service init's `started` report has reached the engine, before the transaction that records `app_instance`; in the kernel lane, the launch stand-in's report (§247). CD3's window |
| `deploy.before_finalizer` | after the transaction that records the attempt's confirmation (journal `confirmed`), before the finalizer's transaction |
| `verify.after_first_read` | after the transaction that records a round's first identity read, before anything else of the round |
| `verify.before_second_read` | once a round's deciding executions are done (the round's step after its checks), before its second identity read is made |

- **D2's launcher barriers for a service launch** (§125; plan §2.3). A service launcher (D2's launcher with the `service` profile, started by the unit) reaches `launcher.before_placement`, `launcher.placed`, `launcher.before_authorization` and `launcher.authorized` as a role's launcher does, armed, listed and released through the same routes. Its wait survives the engine's death, and a later incarnation on the same home lists and releases it (§125). While it waits at `launcher.before_authorization` it has asked nothing; released, it sends its launch request to whatever engine now holds the launch socket.
- **`--harness-clock-offset <seconds>`** †, harness-only (a usage error otherwise, as every harness flag): the engine's controlled clock (§18) starts that many seconds ahead of the host's wall clock; `POST /v1/harness/clock/advance` adds to it. It is how a test restarts an engine near a deadline it moved the clock to (§18 forbids restarting an engine whose clock moved, since an advance does not survive a restart): the test passes the total it advanced. A positive integer; anything else is a usage error.

## 275. The reconcile read as the tests read it

(D4 §2.4, Appendix B `Reconciliation`; D4-A04; §250.) Each entry of `operation_attempts.reconciliation_reads` is `{at, result, read}`: `result` the ReconcileOutcome; **`read.inventory`** † the inventory the outcome was decided from, an array of entries each with at least `resource` (a unit's exact name, or a cgroup, socket or directory path) and `kind` (`unit`, `cgroup`, `socket`, `directory`), so a test can see what was listed; `read.complete` whether the inventory was complete. A read that failed is recorded with `result` `unknown`. **"The receipt deleted"** (M320 (d)) is read as a receipt never recorded: the engine killed at `adapter.after_host_call` †; **"replaced by a false one"** as a receipt that claims `issued` for an effect that changed nothing (§247's `issued` without `apply`), the engine killed at `deploy.receipt_recorded`. Neither writes to the store.

## 276. Decisions on a deploy or teardown operation

(D1 A.8; D4 §§2.4, 4.4, 4.6, 4.7; E112; `../contract/decisions.json`; sections 76 to 82.)

- **`blocker`** (subject_type `operation`, the operation's id). Raised when an attempt is `ambiguous` after a read `conflicting` or `unknown` (D4 §2.4). Its `dependency_manifest` or `question` names the outcome read (the text `conflicting` or `unknown`). It offers **`teardown`** †, the preempting teardown of D4 §4.6 reached through the blocker (the contract's `blocker.options` gains it): answering it makes a `teardown` operation of the environment that takes the lease from the deploy, whose effect stops only what the store positively owns (in the cases, exactly the attempt's unit). What M327 pins of a preemption (the `linked_prior`, `superseded`, `deploy.preempted`, the in-flight call cancelled, the open round recorded `unknown`) is slice 27's; slice 26 reads only that the teardown happens and stops exactly the owned units.
- **`rollout_partial`** † (subject_type `operation`). Raised when an attempt is `reconciled_partial`; no further attempt starts without its answer. Options exactly **`retry`**, **`teardown`**, **`abandon`** (D4 §4.4; no rollback, Q8). Its manifest binds at least `operation_status`, `attempt`, `deployment_generation`, `environment_generation`, `lease_generation`, `config_identity`, `adapter_qualification`, `reconciled` (the read the partial outcome came from), `resources` and `observations` (D1 A.8 with D4 §4.4's list). The `retry` option's `effect_plan` names the bounded remaining effects: the units its cleanup removes and the units it creates, and no other unit. A change to any bound value (the cases change the configuration) stales it: an answer carrying the earlier preview is refused `decision_stale` or `decision_invalidated` (§§76 to 82). Answers: `retry` makes the next attempt (its intent's `cleanup` naming exactly the earlier attempt's units, each `{resource, attempt}` as D4 A.3); `teardown` as the blocker's; **`abandon`** ends the operation `failed` with `outcome_detail` `{"code": "abandoned", …}` †, the authorization still `consumed`, the lease released.
- **The verification ways out** (D4 §4.7). After a verification `failed` or `unknown`, a candidate superseded or a refused completion, the deploy work item waits on a blocker whose reason names the cause (its work read carries the code: `VERIFICATION_FAILED`, `CANDIDATE_SUPERSEDED`, …); re-verification (`POST …/operations/:o/verify`, §266) and an ordinary teardown are then accepted. Which of them a decision row offers is not pinned here.

## 277. Faults and holds of slice 26

Faults of the real adapter, through §262's route (`POST /v1/harness/deploy/faults` `{"environment", "fault"}` → **200**; one-shot; harness-only):

| Fault † | Does |
|---|---|
| `bus_address_missing` | the environment's next reconcile read runs its host calls with the bus address naming a path that does not exist (D4 §2.6 `unreadable`; BS4 §4.1 rule 4); the manager itself is untouched |
| `service_setup_refused` | the environment's next service launcher refuses its own setup (as a mount plan it cannot build) before it asks for a grant, and exits having run nothing |
| `service_exec_failed` | the environment's next service init, granted, fails to `exec` the start command (as an `exec` that returns an error), so the application never starts |
| `service_closure_unread` | the environment's next observation of a service domain's closure (its cgroup's emptiness or absence) fails to read, as `EACCES`; a later observation reads it |
| `control_channel_dropped` | the engine closes its end of the control channel of the environment's current service domain, as if the connection were lost, with no restart |

**`environment_busy`** (D4 §4.5, A.2): a deploy work item waiting for the environment lease names `environment_busy` in its work read (as its blocker's reason or its `dispatch_hold`'s code); an ordinary teardown asked for while the lease is held is not intended until it is released.

## 278. Recovery, ownership, a restored store and supervision

(D4 §§4.1, 4.6, 7.3, 9.2; E110, E116, E126; sections 59, 250, 255, 259, 271.)

- **Launch closure at start.** Before the engine accepts any launch request, every attempt whose launch was granted or authorizable by an earlier incarnation has `launch_state` `closed`; a request from such a launcher is refused and the launcher runs nothing (no `deploy.launch_authorized` for the attempt, no `app_instance`, no application process in the unit's cgroup).
- **Unknown ownership.** A unit whose name carries the environment's prefix and that no attempt intent of the store names, or whose cgroup is not the one the store recorded for it (in the kernel lane the scripted unit's `cgroup`, which the engine records as it records a real unit's `ControlGroup`), is of unknown ownership. Before an effect it fails the precondition `unknown_ownership` (§250); the precondition manifest's `read` for that fact names the unit by its exact name. It is never adopted (no intent, capability or `app_instance` comes from it) and never stopped. Where its reservation cannot be accounted (the recorded cgroup cannot be read), no domain is admitted (a role dispatch stays undispatched).
- **A restored store** (§59; plan §2.6). The test stops the engine in order, takes `surety store backup`, moves `store.db` (and `-wal`, `-shm`) of the same home aside into its own root, runs `surety store restore --from … --bind <project>=<repository>` for every project into that home, and starts the engine again. A "different cgroup" is the restored domain row's `cgroup_path` changed by the test while the engine is stopped (§19's practice).
- **Supervision and the refusal.** A service whose supervision is `unknown` (an engine restart, or the control channel lost) keeps running; its round is `unknown` naming `supervision` (§255); an environment-bound check against it is recorded with `execution_established` 0 and `not_run_reason` **`redaction_unavailable`** (D4 A.2 NotRunReason) and reaches nothing through the link (no `service_link_log` entry, §268). A redeploy makes supervision `attached` and the refusal ends. The refusal of the logs and relay routes (D4 A.8) is slice 27's and 28's (M334 (d)).
- **Accounting** (E126). After a restart, a surviving service domain keeps its reservation `{memory, check_capacity}` (§259), and the one check capacity kept free while any service runs is counted before any admission.
- **A service domain's legal endings** (D4 §9.2, A.4). `execution_domains.status` `terminated` with `terminated_at`, from `launched` or, for a refused setup, directly from `allocated` (`launch_authorized_at` null); `quarantined` while its closure is not observed, keeping its reservation and its launch `closed`, then `terminated` once observed. The application's exit is recorded as **`app_exit`** `{at, status}` on the domain and **`deploy.service_exited`** (`subject.attempt`, `subject.domain`) †, `app_exit.at` no later than `terminated_at` (the plan's "the exit recorded before output is drained": the drain itself is inside the init and is not observed).
- **The environment read** (§255) shows `running` and `supervision` null once the engine's latest read of the environment found nothing of it running (M323 (g): a partial attempt that left nothing), whatever `last_verified` holds.

## 279. CD1's round deadline, and the orchestration deadline's `missing`

(D4 §4.7; E115; E121 CD1; sections 250, 267, 269, 271.) `verification_rounds.deadline_at` † for a round of `POST …/verify` is its `registered_at` plus `deploy_orchestration_deadline`, fixed at registration and never renewed; the round takes the environment lease again (a new `leases` row of kind `environment`) and releases it by §4.7; reaching its deadline records the round's row `unknown` with a `missing` entry of kind `deadline`. The operation's `orchestration_deadline_at` never changes. When the operation's own deadline is reached in verification, the row is `unknown`, `deploy.orchestration_deadline` is emitted once (`subject.operation`), and `missing` holds an entry of kind `deadline` and one for each thing absent: kind `check_execution` for a required check never registered (its `id` the check's †), an entry whose `id` is the execution for a registered execution with no result (quarantined or never admitted; its kind `check_execution` or `check_result`, not pinned), kind `identity_read` for a read not made.

## 280. Names the Verifier fixed in this pass, the readings, and what is deferred

**What this pass changes in earlier sections.** §18's barriers gain §274's; §125's launcher barriers apply to a service launcher; §114's switches gain `--harness-clock-offset`; §247's applying deploy also removes `cleanup` units; §250's attempt reads gain §275's `read.inventory`; §262's fault route gains §277's five faults; §§76 to 82's decision kinds gain `rollout_partial` and `blocker`'s `teardown` (`../contract/decisions.json`; M73 reads the file, so it fails until the engine enables `rollout_partial` with that manifest: the slice-26 straddle).

| What | Fixed as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The kill points' barriers † | §274's six | D4 §4.3's table and plan §2.3's names; `init.app_started` is CD3's window |
| A restart near a deadline † | `--harness-clock-offset` | §18 forbids restarting after a clock advance; D4-O12 asks for a restart near the deadline |
| The recorded inventory † | `read.inventory[].resource`, `kind` | D4-A04 "the same outcome, inventory included" must be observable |
| The receipt deleted / false † | a kill before the receipt; `issued` without `apply` | no store write; both are the adapter's claims lost or wrong |
| `rollout_partial`'s manifest and options † | §276 | D1 A.8 and D4 §4.4 name the bindings and options, not keys |
| `blocker`'s `teardown` † | §276 | D4 §4.6 "through the blocker's teardown option" |
| `abandon`'s outcome † | `outcome_detail.code` `abandoned` | D4 §4.4 names the answer, not the record |
| The five faults † | §277 | plan §2.3 names a missing bus address, a dropped channel; D4 §9.2 a refused setup, a failed `exec`, an unobserved closure |
| `deploy.service_exited`'s subject, `app_exit` † | §278 | D4 A.3, A.5 |
| `unknown_ownership`'s read † | names the unit | D4 §9.2 "lists the unit" |
| `missing` entries at the deadline † | §279 | plan §2.6 leaves the ids to the seam |
| `running` null when nothing runs † | §278 | D4 §4.4 "nothing shown running when nothing is" |

**Readings, each resolved by the design.** (1) M321 (b)'s one Expected sentence ("the service surviving with supervision `unknown`; its round `unknown`…") is read per kill point: where no application was started (placement, the grant) nothing survives and the reading that applies is "no verification passing"; where it was (`started`, verification) all of it applies (D4 §4.3's right-hand column). (2) "A unit of unknown ownership" (M306's deferred case) is a failed precondition before the effect, as M306's Expected says (D4 §4.1, "no unit or domain of the environment is of unknown ownership"), and `conflicting` with a blocker when a reconcile read finds it (D4 §2.4; M320 (e)); both are written. (3) "Restarted by the manager" (M322 (d)) is read as the manager's own restart policy, which D4 §9.2 disables (`Restart=no`, and no second grant after a natural exit); a manager-initiated restart other than by policy would be by hand. (4) M322 (a)'s "after the caller cancelled the create" needs the launch closed for the launcher to be "late"; D4 does not say the cancellation itself closes it, so the case closes it with a restart (D4 §9.2), which D4 does say.

**Deferred** (`../COVERAGE.md`, "M4 slice 26"): M325 (b), an observation during the operation, to slice 27 (the observation job, M329); D4-O13's preempting teardown during verification, to slice 27 (M327 (b)); M324 (a)'s logs and relay refusals, to slice 28 (M334 (d)), their routes being slice 27's and 28's.

## 281. The slice-26 review's S1, and the answers to objections 042 to 045 (2026-10-10)

(The coordinator's ruling on the slice-26 Reviewer's S1, on `build/m4-s26`; D4 §2.4 and §4.6 step 1; `../COVERAGE.md`, "M4 slice 26: the review's S1 and objections 042 to 045".)

- **A teardown's effect waits for the manager's jobs** (S1). Before a teardown's effect, preempting or ordinary, the engine reads the jobs pending under the environment's prefix: the scripted target's `pending_job` in the kernel lane (§247), the manager's job list with the real adapter. If any job is pending, or that read fails, the teardown's attempt is recorded `ambiguous` and no host call is made: no stop, and no `teardown` call in the scripted adapter's call list. The owned unit is left exactly as it was. M321 (g)'s case reaches it through a blocker's `teardown` option, after a read made `unknown` by that same pending job.
- **The scripted adapter's calls are per process** (objection 042). The `calls` of `GET /v1/harness/deploy/environments/:e` are the running engine process's, counted from its start, as slice 23 built them. The target, the queued answers and the admission survive a restart; the calls do not. A case that counts calls across a restart counts only the restarted engine's.
- **A partial attempt superseded by a retry is final** (objection 043; the coordinator's ruling: D4 §2.4 governs over D1 A.5 for deploy attempts). A `reconciled_partial` attempt may move on a reread while it is its operation's latest attempt; once a later attempt of the same operation exists, it is final and needs no open decision.
- **A restored store's own instances** (objection 044). "Never adopted" means no instance is recorded *after* the restore. A store restored from a backup taken after a launch holds that launch's instance, which is not an adoption.
